comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1-C12. Both evaluations find the identification and characterization of METTL3 cleaved forms to be well-supported. OpenEval describes evidence as 'thorough and internally consistent,' while peer reviewers describe it as 'solid' with explicit acknowledgment from all three reviewers.

Perfect agreement on claims C21-C22. Both evaluations accept the characterization of METTL3c and the decision to exclude it from further study. OpenEval notes it as 'a minor technical observation,' while peer reviewers implicitly accept the justification without raising concerns.

Perfect agreement on claims C23-C31. Both evaluations strongly support the proliferation and xenograft rescue experiments. OpenEval describes the logic as 'internally consistent,' while Reviewer 2 explicitly acknowledges the findings and the editor confirms evidence is 'solid.'

Strong agreement on claims C13-C17 (mutagenesis experiments). OpenEval finds evidence 'consistent across multiple experimental systems.' Peer reviewers describe the study as 'properly performed' and molecular assays as 'well-designed,' implicitly accepting these characterization studies. Peer R2 also covers C18-C20 which OpenEval addresses separately in R3.

Agreement on claims C18-C20 regarding METTL3 variant properties. OpenEval notes the in vitro activity doesn't predict in vivo function and rates as SUPPORTED with caveats. Peer reviewers accept these characterization studies as part of the overall 'well-designed' molecular interaction assays without raising specific concerns.

Strong agreement on claims C33-C34, C37-C39 regarding WTAP binding. Both evaluations support the co-IP evidence. OpenEval notes consistency with structural knowledge, while Reviewer 2 explicitly acknowledges METTL3a's role in complex assembly and describes assays as 'well-designed.'

Partial overlap on claims C44-C45. OpenEval R7 addresses C40-C47 on METTL3 self-interaction and sequential assembly, finding evidence SUPPORTED. Peer R4 covers C44-C45 as part of broader acceptance of complex assembly mechanism, described as 'well-designed' and a 'valuable finding.'

Partial overlap on claims C41-C43, C47 regarding self-interaction. OpenEval R7 supports the sequential requirement for self-interaction before WTAP binding. Peer R5 accepts the overall complex assembly model as 'a significant addition to current understanding' without raising concerns about these specific claims.

Strong agreement on claims C48-C50, C52-C55 regarding systematic examination of MTC component depletion. OpenEval supports the hierarchical assembly model. Peer reviewers describe the molecular interaction assays as 'well-designed' and the model as 'a significant addition,' accepting the complex assembly mechanism.

Strong agreement on claims C56-C61 regarding m6A restoration experiments. OpenEval finds evidence 'consistent across overexpression and CRISPR knock-in approaches.' Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge 'reduced m6A level' with METTL3a depletion and confirm evidence is 'solid.'

Strong agreement on claims C62-C63, C66-C68 regarding m6A-seq data. OpenEval describes the analysis as appropriately normalized with dramatic global reduction in m6A peaks. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge the m6A-seq data and confirm evidence is 'solid' without raising concerns.

Strong agreement on claims C69, C71, C73-C77 regarding TMEM127 as key target linking METTL3a to mTOR signaling. OpenEval describes the mechanistic chain as 'well-supported.' Reviewer 2 explicitly acknowledges the TMEM127 mechanism and its effect on proliferation without concerns.

Agreement on claims C133-C135 regarding pathway analysis and TMEM127 validation. OpenEval supports the claims but notes 'primary target' designation (C134) may be overstated. Peer reviewers accept the TMEM127 mechanism without raising this concern, explicitly acknowledging the findings.

Agreement on claims C78, C81-C83 regarding proteasome inhibitor effects. OpenEval supports the evidence from cellular and in vitro systems. Peer reviewers explicitly accept 'METTL3a is generated via 26S proteasome' as part of the overall model without raising concerns about these experiments.

Strong agreement on claims C84-C88 regarding direct proteasome cleavage. OpenEval finds the in vitro reconstitution with purified components 'particularly convincing.' Peer reviewers explicitly accept the proteasome mechanism, with Reviewer 2 stating 'METTL3a is generated via 26S proteasome.'

Strong agreement on claims C90-C93, C95, C97-C99 regarding mTOR-dependent regulation. OpenEval finds evidence for feedback 'strong' though magnitude not quantified. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge the mTOR-dependent mechanism and accept the positive feedback as part of the model.

Partial overlap on claims C103-C104 (feedback loop summary). OpenEval supports the feedback loop but notes relative contribution not quantified. Peer reviewers accept the mTOR-dependent mechanism and feedback, with editor confirming work will be 'of interest to medical biologists.'

Partial overlap on claims C100-C102 (main findings summary). OpenEval supports the integrated findings but notes relative contribution of this mechanism versus other mTOR-m6A connections not quantified. Peer reviewers accept the model as 'a significant addition' with 'solid' evidence.

Agreement on claims C106-C108 regarding mechanistic model. OpenEval supports the model but notes structural details of METTL3a 'bridging' remain speculative. Peer reviewers accept the model as 'a significant addition to current understanding' without raising concerns about speculative elements.

Agreement on claims C138-C139 regarding novelty assertions. OpenEval supports the novelty but notes 'first description' cannot be fully verified without comprehensive literature review. Peer reviewers accept the findings as 'valuable' and a 'significant addition,' implicitly accepting novelty claims.

Divergence on claim C140 (therapeutic implications). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are 'speculative extensions' with no therapeutic validation experiments. Peer reviewers appear to accept the therapeutic potential, with editor noting work will be 'of interest to medical biologists working on breast cancer.'

OpenEval addresses claims C111-C113 regarding METTL3b not generating METTL3a, rating as SUPPORTED but noting inference about N-terminal requirement is indirect. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval rates claims C117-C118 as UNCERTAIN, noting C118 is explicitly speculative about multi-residue motif with no direct evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these claims.

OpenEval rates claims C119-C120 as UNCERTAIN, noting C120 is speculative about tissue-specific variation with no mechanistic investigation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these claims.

OpenEval addresses 30 knowledge claims (C32-C136 selected) referencing prior literature, rating as SUPPORTED with note that detailed verification is beyond scope. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these literature citations.
